description: How two buzzy IPO superstars—Beyond Meat and Oatly—shot to sky-high market caps and then cratered, while legacy food giants quietly held the line. A chart-race of hype vs. shelf reality (2007–2026).
youtube_description:
The Plant-Based Bubble — a Yung Geeski-style chart race of hype vs. reality. Watch Beyond Meat and Oatly explode into headline-grabbing valuations (BYND peaked near its 2019 bubble; OTLY hit blockbuster IPO levels in 2021) — then crash and grind back toward modest sizes. Meanwhile legacy food giants like Tyson and Kellogg stayed comparatively steady, swallowing innovation, buying brands, and cashing in on sustained demand for protein and shelf staples.

What this dataset shows:
- 2019: Beyond Meat’s meteoric valuation spike after the IPO and retail frenzy.
- 2020–2022: A correction across “food tech” as margins, supply-chain shocks and slowing hype hit valuations.
- 2021: Oatly’s IPO moment and post-IPO decline.
- 2022–2026: Legacy players reasserting stability while challengers try to pivot, cut costs and partner with retailers.

If you want B-roll-ready beats, dramatic labels, and an easy-to-read CSV for a chart-race — this timeline is built to jump off the screen.
